title: Make the explainer site introduce Athena and fix newcomer findings
summary: Reworks the generated explainer page (xtask/src/site.rs plus the study's intro and findings text) so a newcomer first learns what Athena is and that this page is an example study of firstmate. It also says who firstmate is for, explains the captain, rewrites the f2 finding in plain words, and adds links to Athena, firstmate and the cited source files. The audience is a newcomer arriving at doodla.github.io/athena.

defaults_applied.how: New rendering behaviour in site.rs gets unit tests, and cargo test and clippy must be clean.
The page is rewritten for an outside reader who has never heard of Athena or firstmate.
Statements about firstmate keep citing claim ids, and nothing new is asserted without a claim.
The fix is made in the generator and the study text, not by hand-editing the output.
One focused change to the site generator and its source text.
No secrets or personal data are added, and the user's email is not written anywhere.
The verifier builds the site and checks the output for the Athena heading and the links.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The Athena repository URL is https://github.com/doodla/athena, inferred from the Pages address doodla.github.io/athena. The producer should confirm it from Cargo.toml or the README.

Every new sentence about firstmate must keep citing a claim, because the generator rejects uncited elements. Sentences about Athena itself are page-level text with an 'about this page' tag, as the glossary already does.

Claim sources link to the pinned commit in the firstmate repository, using repository_url and sha from pin.json. The links are built only when repository_url is a recognisable https GitHub URL, and otherwise the plain text is kept.
The finding that the page does not say who the captain is stays an honest limit. If the study has no claim about the captain, the page says that plainly in newcomer terms instead of inventing facts.
The 2/5 findings are addressed by editing the generator and the study text it renders. The walk-through, which the rater praised, stays as it is.

acceptance_criteria.text: The rendered page's <title> and first heading name Athena, and an opening paragraph says what Athena is, that this page is an example of what its study capability produces, and that firstmate is the system studied.

The 'What firstmate is' section says who uses firstmate and that its workers are AI coding agents. The glossary entry for captain says plainly that it is the human who approves merges, or states what the study does and does not establish about that person. It no longer consists only of 'The text says no more about who the captain is.'

The page has a visible next-step section with clickable links to the Athena repository and to firstmate's repository. Each claim source is a link to its file at the pinned commit rather than a bare file:line string.

The 'Limits of this study' text for finding f2 no longer shows the schema phrase 'guard_evaluated_by for nobody' to the reader. It is reworded in plain language, or the schema field names are explained.

Run `cargo test -p xtask`. The site tests pass, including new tests for the Athena title, the next-step links, the source links and the escaping of link text. Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean.
Run `cargo run -p xtask -- site`. It writes index.html under target/site, and that file contains the Athena heading and the repository links. It does not write inside the work tree.

out_of_scope: Changing the study's claims, model or pinned firstmate commit
Redesigning the page layout or the CSS beyond what the new sections need
Re-running or re-validating the study against firstmate
departures: The cost and time are close to the reference. The change touches generator code, study text and tests together, so I weighted the cost and time slightly higher and the verification pass rate slightly lower.
